purpose: Determine when a citizen should receive a clear notification about a material investigation state change, what happened, why it matters and what action is needed.
core_principle: MATERIAL CHANGE → PLAIN-LANGUAGE NOTICE → WHY IT MATTERS → ACTION IF NEEDED
rules: Notify only for material state changes relevant to the citizen.
Do not notify for every internal processing event.
A notification describes what happened; it does not create a new legal conclusion.
If action is required, state the minimum action clearly.
If no action is required, say so.
Do not expose internal engine states or reasoning.
Do not disclose restricted evidence through notification content.
Do not imply a deadline unless the deadline is verified.
Answer changes must identify whether the change is correction, new evidence, legal change, procedure change or re-verification.
Notification delivery is separate from the underlying investigation state.
hard_stops: Never send a notification solely because an internal stage changed without citizen relevance.
Never expose restricted personal or evidence data.
Never present an unresolved issue as resolved.
Never let notification text alter the underlying investigation record.
